question.question: In the original PREVENT CLOT randomized trial of aspirin versus low-molecular-weight heparin after fractures, aspirin was noninferior for the primary mortality outcome. Which reported secondary-outcome finding is correct?

options.A: Deep-vein thrombosis was 1.71% with aspirin and 2.51% with low-molecular-weight heparin.
options.B: Pulmonary embolism was 2.51% with aspirin and 1.71% with low-molecular-weight heparin.
options.C: Deep-vein thrombosis was 1.49% in both groups.
options.D: Deep-vein thrombosis was 2.51% with aspirin and 1.71% with low-molecular-weight heparin.

action.answer: Deep-vein thrombosis was 2.51% with aspirin and 1.71% with low-molecular-weight heparin.
action.justification: No external evidence was supplied. Based on existing knowledge of the PREVENT trial (comparing aspirin and LMWH in hip fracture patients), aspirin was noninferior for the primary mortality outcome, but the incidence of deep-vein thrombosis (DVT) was 2.51% in the aspirin group and 1.71% in the LMWH group.
